[ASSISTANT_SAID] Networking at career fairs can help individuals improve their knowledge of the job market by meeting industry professionals, learning about job opportunities, building relationships, discovering new technologies and trends, and improving interview skills.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tips for standing out at a career fair include dressing professionally, researching companies, bringing copies of your resume, practicing your elevator pitch, engaging with representatives, following up, and being respectful.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Advice for dealing with nerves at a career fair includes preparing in advance, arriving early, taking breaks, practicing positive self-talk, reminding oneself of goals, and bringing a friend.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommendations for what to wear at a career fair include wearing comfortable shoes, dressing in layers, avoiding flashy clothing, ensuring clothing is neat and clean, choosing light and breathable fabrics, and accessorizing wisely.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Items to bring to the career fair besides copies of the resume include a pen and notepad, business cards, a portfolio, research material, a mobile device, and a bottle of water and a light snack.

[USER] User is considering bringing a friend to the career fair to help them feel more at ease.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It is okay to bring a friend to the career fair, but one should be mindful of distractions and networking opportunities.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] When introducing a friend to company representatives, one should introduce them briefly, explain why they are attending, acknowledge their support, know when to step back, stick to relevant information, and avoid hanging around too long.
